You have all voted against the province of Quebec; and yet, I will remind the hon. member for Yukon (Mr. Nielsen) and the hon. member for the Northwest Territories (Mr. Rheaume) that, yesterday, when they asked something to ensure the respect of their rights, we approved their request. But they have not returned the courtesy.

subtopic: MEASURE TO FACILITATE MAKING LOANS TO STUDENTS
speechtext: Question. Question.

subtopic: MEASURE TO FACILITATE MAKING LOANS TO STUDENTS
speechtext:
You can say "question" as much as you want. As far as I am concerned, I shall say what I have to say until 11.30 p.m.
Yesterday, we spoke to support a measure which did not concern us very much, concerning the respect of the rights of the Yukon and Northwest Territories. But on the vote on clause 12, we did not get the same treatment. As far as clause 15 is concerned, we are not going to benefit therefrom. We are telling the other provinces that we will give them our support to ensure respect of their rights. If they are against the majority, let them vote against the clause, but if they want to vote for it, let them do it, I could not care less.
In any case, the only thing I want to say is that the arguments of the Minister of Public Works as well as those of the Minister of Finance or his parliamentary secretary have not convinced me in any way. They succeeded only in showing me that their arguments did not hold water.
On that, Mr. Chairman, still respectful of the rights of the provinces, I resume my seat before 11.30 so that the bill can be put to a vote. As far as we are concerned, we will not be disturbed for all that. If nine provinces want to give everything to the central government in Ottawa, let them do it. Then, only one province will have safeguarded its own rights, and the nine others will be in tow of the federal government.
In short, the province of Quebec will be the second, because then there will only be associate provinces. We shall be able to discuss together certain matters of common concern to all, but there will be only one province, namely the province of Quebec, and nine other provinces which will really make one, so that, living side by side, we shall be able to co-operate with one another, enjoying rights conferred on us by a new constitution. Then, we shall form a new Canada.

(a) enter into arrangements with any department, branch or agency of the government of Canada or any other public or private organization or agency to assist the minister in carrying out the purposes and provisions of this act;
I hope the minister will not enter into any kind of arrangement with public or private organizations in the province of Quebec, that he will not interfere in a matter where he has no business, especially in the field of education. I hope clause 16 will not allow him to do that.
I would like to have the assurance of the minister in that matter.

speechtext: The purpose is to permit the government to enter into agreements with any universities that may be delegated to act on behalf of the provincial authorities, and I can guarantee that if Quebec does not come in under this plan we will not be making any agreements with universities or any other private bodies in Quebec.

subtopic: MEASURE TO FACILITATE MAKING LOANS TO STUDENTS
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I would still have a small question to ask. It should not take long, just a couple of minutes.
[The Chairman.]
A year ago, when we were dealing with municipal loans and, I believe, an amount of $400 million, I asked the Minister of Finance if he could not go and get the required credit from the Bank of Canada. Now, the Minister of Finance, or rather the Minister of Trade and Commerce (Mr. Sharp), who was in charge at that time, replied that such a thing would not be possible for as large an amount as $400 million.
But since today we are only dealing with a small amount of $2 million a year, perhaps the Minister of Finance would be willing to make a test and go and get the required credit, not in the taxpayers' pockets in the form of taxes, but from the Bank of Canada?
The amount involved is small since it is only $2 million.
In 1939, at the beginning of the war, the Minister of Finance of the Liberal government got $200 million to place the country on a war footing. The present Minister of Finance would perhaps agree to go and get this small amount of $2 million from the Bank of Canada. I should like to have his comment on that point.

speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I lodge a vigorous protest at this rearrangement of the business of the house, after we have been told time and time again that these legislative items would come before interim supply. Surely the government can stick to a program for two or three days?
